// diagnostic

E0622

A module binding's value must be a literal

What

A module binding's value must be a literal

Why

A mutable or `#Persist` module global is runtime storage, which every execution tier initializes from a scalar literal before `fn run`. An immutable `::` constant may compute its value: the build folds it when it can and computes it at startup otherwise.

Fix

Use an integer, float, or bool literal, or keep a computed value in an immutable `::` constant.

Worked example

First UI snapshot mentioning E0622: tests/ui/module_array_computed_element.stderr.

Error [jet.ModuleGlobalNotLiteral]: A module binding's value must be a literal
  --> tests/ui/module_array_computed_element.jet:1:14
    |
  1 | bad_table := [Int]{1 + 2}
    |              ^^^^^^^^^^^^
 Why: A mutable or `#Persist` module global is runtime storage, which every execution tier initializes from a scalar literal before `fn run`
 Fix: Use an integer, float, or bool literal, or keep struct and list values in an unmarked `::` constant
